summary.headline: Indiqube Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR428 crore (+37% YoY) and PAT rose 91% to INR35 crore, with PAT margin at 8%.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR428 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA of INR87 crore (+34%), EBIT of INR55 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR35 crore (+91%). Margins expanded, with EBIT margin at 13% (11% a year ago) and PAT margin at 8% (6%). Rent-paying area was flat QoQ, which management attributed to the timing of building handovers, with about 2 million sq ft of annual additions still guided. Q&A centred on VAS revenue (INR39 crore one-time in the quarter), solar capex, a large new Noida centre, and occupancy and margin ranges. Management declined to give quarterly OCF or capex figures ahead of the H1 audit.

segments.name: Client mix (revenue)
segments.commentary: GCCs ~52-53% of revenue, startups and unicorns ~23%, Indian enterprises ~28% (of which GCCs ~10-12%). Multi-center clients ~41% of revenue; top five clients 12% of revenue; 855 clients as of June 2026.

segments.name: VAS (DesignQube, IndiCare, Eco)
segments.commentary: VAS is ~17% of revenue and management expects it to rise by about 2-4 percentage points. VAS EBIT margin is guided at ~15% for the next one to two years, as growth takes priority over margin.

segments.name: Solar / sustainability
segments.commentary: About 30 MW of solar capacity is operational. Plan to add 25-30 MW this year at INR100-120 crore capex; solar IRR stated at 18-22%.

guidance_outlook: Annual additions of close to 2 million sq ft (about 44,000 seats) reiterated; about 3.9 million sq ft (about 97,000 seats) of headroom already signed.
Corporate occupancy guided at 80-85% (stated later as 82-86%); mature centres (over 12 months) at 85-90% (stated as 86-90%/88-90%).
Margin ranges guided at EBITDA 19-21%, EBIT 11-13%, PAT 8-10% on a annual basis.
Operational break-even for new centres is 5-6 months at about 52-57% occupancy; steady state around 12 months (9-12 months to reach ~90%).
Around 2.8 million sq ft of area under management not yet rent-paying is expected to become operational in 12-16 months (most signed supply to deliver in 12-18 months).
Large Noida centre expected to go live around mid-2027 (Q2 or Q3 FY28).
Management expects to sign larger spaces in Hyderabad and Mumbai during this financial year.
capex_capacity: Solar: 30 MW operational; plan to add 25-30 MW this year at INR100-120 crore capex.
Capex and OCF for Q1 not disclosed; management said figures would be provided with H1 results after audit and review. Capex is driven by interiors, design-and-build, solar and vendor payment cycles.
Debt increase is attributed to solar investment, not the leasing business (per Vikas Agarwal).
New Noida centre is a large single building; live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28).
demand_pricing: Institutional supply share rose to ~20% of portfolio from ~12% a couple of years ago; institutional buildings carry higher rents and CAM costs but management says margins are consistent across supply types.
Tier-2 centres: real estate cost INR50-70 per sq ft; seat pricing INR6,500-7,500 per seat; unit economics said to be similar to Tier-1.
Bangalore is ~60-64% of area; Chennai ~10%. Management expects Bangalore share to fall as NCR, Hyderabad, Mumbai and West India grow.
Attrition is negative (net expansion); client renewal rate ~90%; client notice periods 60-90 days; leases are straight leases with landlords (no back-to-back).
Tech parks are ~20% of portfolio. North Bangalore exposure is under 0.5 million sq ft of ~6.5 million sq ft in Bangalore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no QoQ rise in rent-paying area despite 2 million sq ft annual guidance, and is supply slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said additions are lumpy and tracked annually; H2 FY26 added ~1.14 million sq ft. No slowdown is seen, and ~3.9 million sq ft of signed headroom is available.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR39 crore one-time VAS revenue and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue came across DesignQube, IndiCare and Eco. Management said it is non-recurring in quarters but will keep recurring over time, with VAS share rising 2-4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How much solar capex is planned and what IRR is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25-30 MW more at INR100-120 crore; solar IRR 18-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the large Noida centre and is it demand-backed?
qa_highlights.answer: Live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28). Management said it was largely proactive supply, not pre-leased, based on NCR micro-market research.

qa_highlights.question: Will new centres dilute margins given slow break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational break-even takes 5-6 months at 52-57% occupancy and steady state ~12 months, so no margin pressure expected. The 36 months referred to full capex recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What margin will VAS deliver and will it drive group margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: VAS margin ~15% for the next one to two years; management prioritises scale. Group-level margins are expected to stay within the stated ranges.

risks_watch: Rent-paying area was flat QoQ; the ~2 million sq ft annual addition depends on H2-weighted handovers in Jan-Feb.
Revenue concentration: Bangalore ~60% of area; the Noida site is a large non-institutional asset held by an HNI family group.
Capex and OCF not disclosed for Q1; H1 numbers due after audit.
One-time VAS revenue (INR39 crore) inflates the quarter; the underlying run-rate needs checking.
Interest cost rising with solar-linked debt; watch debt quantum and cost in H1 disclosures.
Occupancy guidance has been stated in different ranges during the call (corporate 80-85% vs 82-86%); clarify the official range.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, pipeline and margin stability, with specific ranges given. Evasive on quarterly capex, OCF and city-wise revenue-to-rent ratio, deferring these to H1 audited numbers.

key_quotes: Q1 27 marks a very strong start for the year with Indiqube delivering its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR428 crores representing growth of 37 % year-on-year.
We have consistently said that we intend to add close to 2 million square feet every year and we remain committed to that growth trajectory.
So, it's not about 36 months. 36 months is the full capex recovery we are talking about. But my break-even is within five to six months.

And both capex and cash flow both, you know, we internally really calculated but we prefer not to give the provisional number at this stage since the number will be subject to the H1 audit and review.

So, the focus is to scale and grow more than the margin expansion. So, our margin in my VAS revenue would be around about 15% and you know and this is going to be like this for the next one or two years at least

25-30 MW solar capacity addition (captive/sustainability, not leasing space)

growth.why: Q1 revenue +37% YoY and EBITDA +34%, with guidance to add ~2 million sq ft a year (about 3.9 million sq ft signed headroom), utilisation at 86%, and a 25-30 MW solar addition at INR100-120 crore; however, Q1 revenue includes a one-time INR39 crore VAS recognition and rent-paying area was flat QoQ, so the run-rate is less clear.
